question: In which year were the Arms Act and Vernacular Press Act passed?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1878**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Arms Act** and the **Vernacular Press Act** were both enacted in the year **1878**.
 
• The **Arms Act** was designed to restrict the possession of arms by the Indian population, requiring them to obtain a license for the ownership of weapons.
 
• The **Vernacular Press Act** was implemented to curtail the freedom of the Indian-language press, allowing the colonial government to clamp down on publications that were critical of British policies.
 
• These acts were part of a series of measures taken by the British colonial authorities to tighten control over the Indian populace and suppress dissent.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Vernacular Press Act** was specifically aimed at curbing the influence of the Indian press, which was becoming increasingly vocal in its criticism of British rule.
 
• The act allowed the government to confiscate the printing press, paper, and other materials of any publication that published content deemed seditious.
 
• The **Arms Act** was part of the colonial strategy to prevent the possibility of armed rebellion following the Revolt of 1857.
 
• These acts were widely criticized by Indian leaders and intellectuals as unjust and repressive measures that stifled the rights and freedoms of the Indian people.
